analyst_view.overall: Bottom-three Sassuolo (18th, 8 points) host Napoli (8th, 18 points). Sassuolo have lost six league games in a row and conceded 21 goals in that run; Roberto D'Aversa replaced the sacked Alberto Aquilani on 10 November and lost his first game 2-0 to Genoa, and he is moving to a back three (3-4-3 expected) to tighten up. Napoli come in from a 2-2 at Manchester City on Tuesday under a coach, Massimiliano Allegri, who is under pressure, with a long injury list: Meret, Badiashile, Di Lorenzo, Lobotka, Vergara and Alisson Santos (in the numbers) plus Buongiorno (out until January, not in the numbers). Sassuolo are also without Adzic, Volpato and Leysen (counted) and Boloca and Kone (not counted), with Bakola doubtful. No referee has been named yet; I lean slightly lower on goals and shots for a tired, thin Napoli after a Champions League night and a new coach's tighter Sassuolo shape.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals (0.8 Sassuolo, 1.7 Napoli) and already add Sassuolo's 21 goals conceded in six games and take off the injured players on both sides. Much of that leaking came under Aquilani, and D'Aversa is switching to a back three for more cover, while Napoli play five days after a draining 2-2 at Manchester City with a thin squad, so I lean mildly lower to about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners and already add some for Sassuolo because Napoli have conceded 41 corners in their last six games. A deeper Sassuolo back three could hand Napoli more corners while Sassuolo's wing-backs push less, but nothing clear points either way, so I stay at about 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards and already take a little off for Sassuolo's low card count lately. A side in a relegation fight under a new coach can play with more edge, but no referee has been named and I found nothing pointing to a heated game, so I stay at about 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.3 shots and already add +8% for Napoli's recent shooting against a Sassuolo side that conceded 105 shots in six games. Napoli are short of legs after Tuesday at the Etihad with Lobotka, Vergara and Neres out and Allegri's sides tend to manage games, so I trim mildly to about 26.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target and already add +13% for Napoli's accuracy in their last six games, while Sassuolo have managed only 17 on target in that run. For the same reasons as shots, a tired Napoli and a more compact Sassuolo, I trim mildly to about 9.0.
